notes: Building and Industrial News, vol. 14 part 2 (Internet Archive buildingindustri14214cont), the 27 weekly issues from 1 July to 30 December 1914; the paper changed its title to Building and Engineering News with the issue of 9 December 1914, and the last four issues are cited under that title. Same method as the Building and Engineering News run (source building-engineering-news), which this volume immediately precedes: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll year fits, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before the work. The issues were dated from their covers (every Wednesday). The labels are printed with leader dots; the OCR loses some item numbers, so extract.py ran with BEN_LOOSE=1, the item numbers of the published rows were read from the page image, and unresolved rows whose number was not read carry no extra.item and say so in the locator. Every published row was read against the page image, location first; a cost or name not legible on the image, or past a column break, was left out. Owners who are private individuals are never recorded, nor is a contractor or architect who is the owner, shares the owner's surname, or is listed at the owner's premises; sureties are cut. Held back at the image: storey, unit or use counts that contradict the roll, minor work (electric signs, underpinning, small repairs), small alterations and plain single houses on parcels with no page (held for a page), rows of houses on one listing, and entries cut off by a column break. One alteration printed as 'No. 253 Fourth' was held because the street or the avenue could be meant; one entry (the caissons at California and Stockton) was held because the page already credits other architects for the building on the parcel the corner resolves to. One held fact of the later run (136 Jordan Avenue, 29 November 1930) was read against its page image and taken up when this volume seeded the page.

coverage.remaining: Unread: the six earlier half-year volumes on the Internet Archive (vol. 11 pt. 1, 1911, to vol. 13 pt. 2, July to December 1913). In this volume: 198 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; they still need the image check), and 14 more were held for a page at the image. 347 rows have a nearest parcel that was not accepted. 681 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today. Two contracts for the apartment house at Taylor and Sacramento sit on a parcel with no address row.
coverage.note: 2,231 numbered entries read, 1,416 San Francisco rows, 735 placed on a parcel, 204 picked and read against the page image, 149 published on 134 pages (52 seeded), 53 held back at the image.
